newsitem.title: FRANCE: French centre right gains slightly in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: French centre right gains slightly in latest poll.

text.p: Support for France's governing centre-right coalition rose by one percentage point, while the left's standing was stable, a poll released on Monday showed.

A coalition of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist Rally for the Republic and the centrist Union for French Democracy would take 40 percent of the vote, up one percentage point from two weeks earlier, the poll by Louis Harris for Valeurs Actuelle showed.
The Socialists would take 26.5 percent of the vote, a 0.5 percentage point increase, the poll showed.
The Communist party's showing fell by one percentage point to nine percent and the left of centre environmentalists rose by 0.5 point to 8.5 percent in the standings.
Two percent would vote for the extreme left party, unchanged from the previous poll. The combined percentage of left of centre parties would reach 46 percent of the vote.
The sampling of 951 people over 18 taken on April 18 and 19 showed that Jean-Marie Le Pen's far-right National Front would receive 14 percent of the vote, down a percentage point.
Twenty percent had not decided who to vote for and 31 percent of those expressing a preference said they could still change their mind.
